label: Currency Exchange Business Registration
kw: Currency exchange business registration agent in Korea
answer: Currency exchange business registration (환전업무 등록) is a specialized foreign exchange business registration that a person other than a financial institution must obtain in advance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (외국환거래법) to buy and sell foreign currency as a business. Registration authority is delegated to the Commissioner of the Korea Customs Service (관세청장), so applications are received in practice by the customs office with jurisdiction over the business premises. The legal requirements are two — business premises needed for currency exchange and the computer systems set by notice — and there is no minimum capital requirement. After registration, anti-money laundering duties such as customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting apply. YouSun Administrative Agency prepares and files the registration application and attachments.

glance.label: Who needs it
glance.value: Sole proprietors and corporations, other than financial institutions, that intend to buy or sell foreign currency, or buy traveler's checks issued abroad, as a business

glance.label: Requirements
glance.value: Business premises needed for currency exchange, computer systems set by notice of the Minister of Economy and Finance, and no grounds for disqualification of the applicant (including officers for a corporation) (persons within 3 years of registration cancellation are barred)

glance.label: Process
glance.value: Check disqualification grounds → prepare business premises and computer systems → file for registration (received by the competent customs office) → review of premises, computer systems, documents and disqualification → registration certificate issued → anti-money laundering compliance and change or discontinuation reports

glance.label: Documents
glance.value: Currency exchange business registration application (stating name, business location, scope of business and officers), proof of business premises (lease agreement, etc.), proof of computer systems, corporate register extract (corporations), copy of business registration certificate, officers' disqualification check documents (corporations)

glance.label: Timeline
glance.value: The foreign exchange laws and regulations set no statutory processing period, so timing depends on the checks of the business premises and computer systems and on supplementation

chooser.label: Opening an exchange counter as a sole proprietor
Moving the office or closing the business
Questions about customer checks and reporting after registration

situations.q: I want to open a currency exchange business in Korea. Do I register with the customs office rather than the Ministry of Economy and Finance?
situations.conclusion: By the wording of the law, the registering authority is the Minister of Economy and Finance, but the authority for currency exchange registration and change or discontinuation reports is delegated to the Commissioner of the Korea Customs Service, who may further delegate part of it to heads of customs offices. In practice, applications are received by the customs office with jurisdiction over the business location.

branches.when: Your business location is decided
branches.then: Confirm the filing route with the customs office for that location and submit the registration application.

branches.when: You are supervised or inspected after registration
branches.then: Supervision and inspection are also carried out by the Commissioner of the Korea Customs Service, and joint inspections with the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service may take place if there are concerns about harm to market order.

situations.docs: Currency exchange business registration application, proof of business premises, proof of computer systems, copy of business registration certificate
situations.period: In practice, depends on the competent customs office's checks of the premises and computer systems and on supplementation (no statutory processing period)

situations.q: Can I register a currency exchange business in Korea as a sole proprietor without setting up a corporation?
situations.conclusion: Yes. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act provides for registration by persons other than financial institutions, and the officer details in the application are limited to corporations, so sole proprietors can also register.

branches.when: You are a sole proprietor
branches.then: Apply with a copy of your business registration certificate, identification documents, and evidence of business premises and computer systems.

branches.when: You are a corporation
branches.then: Add the corporate register extract, articles of incorporation, officer details and officers' disqualification check documents.

situations.docs: Currency exchange business registration application, copy of business registration certificate, identification documents, proof of business premises, proof of computer systems
situations.period: In practice, depends on the checks of the premises and computer systems and on whether supplementation is needed

situations.q: Can a currency exchange business be registered in an ordinary shopping arcade, not a special tourist zone or airport?
situations.conclusion: The Enforcement Decree only requires business premises needed for currency exchange and does not restrict location. However, whether the premises genuinely exist (signage, counter, storage equipment and so on) and whether the computer systems meet the notice are substantively reviewed.

branches.when: You have secured a separate business space
branches.then: Prove the premises with a lease agreement or similar, set up the computer systems, and apply.

branches.when: You want to place a counter inside a store in another line of business
branches.then: First check whether you can show that the exchange premises genuinely exist.

situations.docs: Lease agreement or register extract for the premises, photos and layout of the premises, proof of computer systems, registration application
situations.period: In practice, depends on the premises inspection schedule

situations.q: How long does currency exchange business registration in Korea take, from application to the registration certificate?
situations.conclusion: The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree set no statutory processing period for currency exchange registration. If the requirements are met and no grounds for refusal apply (inadequate premises or computer systems, defective documents, disqualification, or violation of other laws), registration must be granted, so the completeness of your documents drives the timeline.

branches.when: Your evidence of premises and computer systems is complete
branches.then: The registration certificate is issued after review, and anti-money laundering duties apply from that point.

branches.when: Supplementation is requested due to defective documents or inadequate equipment
branches.then: Registration is delayed until the supplementation is completed.

situations.docs: Currency exchange business registration application, proof of business premises, proof of computer systems, corporate register extract (corporations)
situations.period: No statutory processing period / In practice, depends on the competent customs office's checks and supplementation

situations.q: I'm looking into the cost of currency exchange business registration in Korea. Do I need a minimum capital?
situations.conclusion: Currency exchange business has no legal minimum capital requirement; the registration requirements are business premises and the computer systems set by notice. However, measures such as a deposit or insurance or mutual aid enrollment may be imposed after registration.

branches.when: You have not prepared the premises and computer systems yet
branches.then: First lease the premises and set up the computer systems required by the notice.

branches.when: You have been ordered to make a deposit or take out insurance
branches.then: Failing to comply is a ground for registration cancellation or business suspension, so comply within the deadline.

situations.docs: Lease agreement for the premises, proof of computer systems, currency exchange business registration application, copy of business registration certificate
situations.period: In practice, time to prepare the premises and computer systems is needed first

situations.q: If our currency exchange counter also wants to offer overseas money transfers, do we need a separate registration?
situations.conclusion: Yes. The Enforcement Decree requires separate registration for each business when combining currency exchange, small-sum overseas remittance and other specialized foreign exchange businesses.

branches.when: You only buy and sell foreign currency
branches.then: Currency exchange business registration is sufficient.

branches.when: You also handle payments and receipts between Korea and other countries
branches.then: You need a separate small-sum overseas remittance business registration, with different requirements and procedures.

situations.docs: Currency exchange business registration application, small-sum overseas remittance business registration application (if combined), documents required by notice for each business
situations.period: In practice, each business is reviewed separately

situations.q: How do we move our currency exchange counter to a new location or expand the currencies we handle?
situations.conclusion: If the name, business location or scope of currency exchange business changes, you must file a change report at least 7 days before the change. Conducting foreign exchange business without a change report or with a false report is subject to a fine of up to KRW 100 million.

branches.when: You are relocating the business
branches.then: File the change report with evidence of the new premises at least 7 days before the move.

branches.when: You want to go beyond the scope set at registration
branches.then: File a change report for the scope of business in advance.

situations.docs: Change report, lease agreement for the new premises (if relocating), proof of the change, registration certificate
situations.period: Statutory: report at least 7 days before the change

situations.q: Do we have to report separately to customs to close our currency exchange business?
situations.conclusion: To discontinue foreign exchange business, you must file a discontinuation report at least 7 days before the discontinuation date, and failing to do so is subject to a fine.

branches.when: You are stopping currency exchange completely
branches.then: Submit the discontinuation report at least 7 days before the planned date.

branches.when: You are stopping currency exchange but continuing another specialized foreign exchange business
branches.then: Registration is per business, so file a discontinuation report for currency exchange only.

situations.docs: Discontinuation report, registration certificate, documents required by notice
situations.period: Statutory: report at least 7 days before the discontinuation date

situations.q: After registering a currency exchange business in Korea, how do we verify customer identity and report transactions?
situations.conclusion: A registered currency exchange operator counts as a financial institution under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (특정금융정보법) and must carry out customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, currency transaction reporting (within 30 days when cash at or above the amount set by Presidential Decree is exchanged), and appoint a reporting officer, set internal guidelines and train staff.

branches.when: A one-off transaction at or above a set amount occurs
branches.then: Verify the customer's identity and beneficial owner.

branches.when: A transaction is suspected of involving illegal proceeds
branches.then: Report it to the Commissioner of the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit without delay and do not tell the counterparty about the report.

situations.docs: Reporting officer appointment documents, internal guidelines, customer due diligence records, transaction report records
situations.period: Statutory: currency transaction reports within 30 days, suspicious transaction reports without delay

situations.q: Our currency exchange registration was cancelled in the past. Can we register again in Korea?
situations.conclusion: You cannot register again until 3 years have passed from the date of cancellation. This restriction also applies to officers and employees of a cancelled corporation who were responsible for the grounds for cancellation, and officers are also reviewed for disqualification when a corporation applies.

branches.when: 3 years have passed since cancellation
branches.then: Set up the premises and computer systems again and file a new registration application.

branches.when: A person within the 3-year period is an officer of a new corporation
branches.then: That corporation's registration may be refused, so review the officer lineup first.

situations.docs: Currency exchange business registration application, officers' disqualification check documents, evidence of premises and computer systems
situations.period: Statutory: re-registration restricted for 3 years from the cancellation date

situations.q: If we hire an administrative agent for currency exchange business registration in Korea, what exactly do they handle?
situations.conclusion: We handle pre-checks of disqualification grounds, premises and computer systems, preparation of the registration application and scope of business, filing with the competent customs office and supplementation responses, and post-registration change and discontinuation reports. Whether to register is decided by the competent authority.

branches.when: You are opening a new exchange counter
branches.then: After checking the requirements, we tell you which evidence is missing, then prepare and file the documents.

branches.when: You need to build AML internal controls, assess the legality of foreign exchange transactions, or lease premises
branches.then: We do not handle these, so the business owner proceeds directly or with the relevant institutions.

situations.docs: Business registration certificate or corporate register extract, lease agreement for the premises, evidence of computer systems
situations.period: In practice, depends on document preparation and the customs office's inspection schedule

glossary.def: A person, other than a financial institution, that has completed currency exchange business registration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act to buy and sell foreign currency as a business.

Foreign exchange business that a person other than a financial institution may conduct on condition of registration, divided into currency exchange, small-sum overseas remittance and other specialized foreign exchange business.

glossary.term: Scope of currency exchange business (환전업무의 취급 범위)
glossary.def: The scope of currency exchange business stated in the registration application. A change report is required to change it.

The two registration requirements for currency exchange: business premises needed for currency exchange, and the computer systems set by notice of the Minister of Economy and Finance for currency exchange and follow-up management.
Reports filed at least 7 days before the date when changing the name, business location or scope of business, or discontinuing the business.

A specialized foreign exchange business of making and receiving payments between Korea and other countries and the related buying and selling of foreign currency, registered separately from currency exchange.

glossary.term: Financial institution for AML purposes (금융회사등, 자금세탁방지)
glossary.def: An institution with duties under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, such as suspicious transaction reporting, currency transaction reporting and customer due diligence. Registered currency exchange operators fall into this category.
The duty to verify a customer's identity and beneficial owner when opening a new account or conducting a one-off financial transaction at or above a set amount.
